# FIX-ORI-SUITE-1: Repair the pre-existing suite breaks on trunk

## What this does

Repairs the seven pre-existing test-suite breaks on trunk — each planner-verified failing on trunk `ca759bd7` independent of any reporting task — so ORI-CI-003/ORI-CI-004's aggregate `pnpm test` acceptance can pass and the shared search-selector class stops failing the Playwright lane. Every repair lives in the seven named test files plus one task-owned proof harness (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/suite-repair-proof.test.ts`) that verifies each named selection now passes; NO product source changes.

The seven verified breaks and their repairs:

1. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/single-tutorial-gate.test.ts` — 3 pass / 2 fail (`ORI-CI-001-duplicate` at :461, `ORI-CI-001-noncanonical` at :496). Since ORI-CI-002's ordered chain, `check:snippets` runs before Astro's tutorial gate, and the drill's copied/renamed Quickstart carries four source-bound blocks with no committed binding, so the build stops at `[authored-snippets] no committed binding (unbound source-bound block): document apps/docs/src/content/docs/ori-ci-001-second-tutorial.mdx …` before `[docs-data] single-tutorial` can speak — the unpublished draft variant trips it too. Repair: the drill's `runDuplicateCases`/`runNoncanonicalCase` extend (duplicate) or re-point (noncanonical) the SCRATCH copy's `COMMITTED_BINDINGS` in `scripts/docs-data/authored-snippets.ts` for the copy's four source-bound blocks — exactly ORI-CI-002's duplicate-tutorial insertion pattern (`docs-build-pipeline.test.ts` `planDuplicateTutorial`) — restored byte-exactly in the drill's finally. The noncanonical rename must RE-POINT the four quickstart entries (not just add): the stale-binding check at `authored-snippets.ts:945` (`stale binding: … matches no authored block and no emitted element`) rejects the orphaned quickstart bindings once the file is renamed.
2. `tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/scaffold.build.test.ts` — 1 pass / 1 fail (`FUSE-01-manifest-contract` at :142: `dependency "github-slugger" is outside the TR-06 allowed set`; `wrangler` is the next offender behind it; then :162-163 pins the retired three-segment build script). Repair: extend the TR-06 allowed set with exactly the two landed dependencies (`github-slugger`, landed by ORI-AST-001 `bf202aac`; `wrangler`, landed by ORI-DEP-001 `57903f51`) with a supersede comment naming both commits, and supersede the build-script pin to the landed seven-stage public-build form (ORI-CI-002's `ci-chain-order` supersede is the pattern; `STAGE_ORDER` in `docs-build-pipeline.test.ts` is the living contract).
3. `tests/sprint-04-generated-reference/data-table-contract.test.ts` — 3 pass / 1 fail (`:58 rows prop is the required readonly cell-matrix`). AST-007's rich-cell form made `rows` optional (`rows?: readonly { text: string; mono?: boolean }[][]`) and moved the loop to `rows?.map(` with the default-slot rich body. Repair: update the `rows:` regex to the optional form, assert the rich-body slot branch alongside, and re-anchor the exactly-1 loop count to `rows?.map(`.
4. `tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/ledger.spec.ts` — failures across its tokens (planner-verified: 112 `rnr-copy-button button` triggers — two labeled engine commands per row since AST-007; strict-mode on the bulk-add `code` pair — the standalone display `<code>` plus the CopyButton island's internal `code`; `td.ledger-type` now renders the stripped category; `td.ledger-verdict` replaced by the Badge in a plain `td`; `table.ledger__table` replaced by `table.data-table` under `.ledger-table__scroll` with `tbody[data-ledger]`; the Docs column now links `/components/{name}` for all 56 rows via `a[data-docs-link]`). Repair: rewrite the selectors to AST-007's landed LedgerTable shape, adopting the living sprint-05 lane precedents (`ledger-presentation.spec.ts`: row-scoped `.badge`, `[data-engine-command="nativewind"] rnr-copy-button`, `a[data-docs-link]`); retire only the assertions superseded by living sprint-05 lanes (the in-page `#row-` docs-href fragment scheme — every row now has a real ORI-AST-008 destination), and keep rewriting everything that still guards real sprint-01 behavior: 56 rows name-for-name against the generated dataset, verdict vocabulary, absolute-URL command regex, clipboard equality, DOM-order, and the no-JS render.
5. `tests/sprint-03-family-browse/verdict-badge-wiring.spec.ts` — 6 pass / 3 fail (token `FAM-005-ledger-badge-wiring` times out in all three projects): same replaced-selector class (`td.ledger-verdict .badge`, `td.ledger-docs a`, the `#row-` docs-href helper, and the per-row copy count now 2 per row). Repair: same selector rewrite; the `id="row-{name}"` anchor assertions stay (the anchors survive on the `tr`).
6. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/not-found-search-recovery.spec.ts` — 6 pass / 3 fail (the two JS-enabled projects' AC tokens at :488/:706): strict-mode violation `locator('[data-search-slot] button') resolved to 2 elements` — VIS-003's `data-search-close` button landed inside the header slot next to the trigger. Repair: the one-line selector fix, scoping to the trigger's specific selector `'[data-search-slot] button.search-dialog__trigger'` — the exact form the living `search-presentation.spec.ts:40` already uses.
7. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/search-contract.spec.ts` — 5 pass / 10 fail (every JS-enabled token — the locked 13-step sequence and AC-1..AC-4 — in chromium-desktop and chromium-mobile fails at the :208 click on the same strict-mode violation; the no-JS project passes). Same one-line class and same repair as member 6: `SEARCH_TRIGGER` becomes `'[data-search-slot] button.search-dialog__trigger'`; nothing else in the spec changes.

Planner-verified trunk observations recorded 2026-09-25 on `ca759bd7`: single-tutorial-gate 3/2, scaffold.build 1/1, data-table-contract 3/1, ledger.spec failing, verdict-badge-wiring 6/3, not-found-search-recovery 6/3, search-contract 5/10 (all via the exact per-suite selectors preserved below).

## Why

ORI-CI-003 and ORI-CI-004 are the sprint's CI acceptance owners and their aggregate `pnpm test` gate cannot exit 0 while the vitest-class members fail on trunk and the shared search-selector class fails the Playwright lane, through no fault of theirs. Each break is collateral of landed, reviewed sprint-05 work (ORI-CI-002's ordered chain, ORI-AST-001/DEP-001's dependencies, AST-007's rich-cell ledger, AST-008's per-item destinations, VIS-003's close button) that legitimately moved the product past suites pinned to the older shape. The owning tasks of those suites are all completed, ORI-CI-002 (the ordered-build owner — completed, approved `3573a237`, merged `c9bb5cc5`) has landed, and no pending task owns the repair. The wave-19 decision (source item `ORI-VIS-004:7230130b…:scope_impact:1`, handoff sha256 `4630af86…`) authorized exactly this add.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run tests/sprint-05-orient-search/suite-repair-proof.test.ts
pnpm test
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci tests/sprint-05-orient-search/single-tutorial-gate.test.ts tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/scaffold.build.test.ts tests/sprint-04-generated-reference/data-table-contract.test.ts tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/ledger.spec.ts tests/sprint-03-family-browse/verdict-badge-wiring.spec.ts tests/sprint-05-orient-search/not-found-search-recovery.spec.ts tests/sprint-05-orient-search/search-contract.spec.ts tests/sprint-05-orient-search/suite-repair-proof.test.ts
```

The first command is the exact selector: the task-owned proof harness spawns each of the seven preserved per-suite selectors (three vitest, four Playwright after one real `pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs` build), asserts exit 0 for each, runs `pnpm typecheck` and the scoped Biome command, and asserts the tracked-file diff boundary — recording RED (the planner-verified trunk failures, bound to the pre-change candidate SHA) and GREEN (per-suite exit 0) in `.tmp/FIX-ORI-SUITE-1/`. `pnpm test` (the aggregate vitest run), `pnpm typecheck`, and the scoped Biome command are preserved GREEN commands the implementer runs and records in `run.json`; the harness never spawns `pnpm test` itself (a vitest child spawning the vitest aggregate would re-run every drill and the harness — unbounded recursion).

## Scope

Own exactly the seven named test files, the task-owned proof harness, drill-emitted evidence appends, and bounded `.tmp/FIX-ORI-SUITE-1/` evidence. Zero product-source changes: the single-tutorial repair mutates `scripts/docs-data/authored-snippets.ts` ONLY inside the drill's owned `os.tmpdir()` scratch copies (restored byte-exactly in the drill's finally — the ORI-CI-002 duplicate-tutorial mutation pattern); `apps/docs/src/components/DataTable.astro`, `LedgerTable.astro`, `Badge.astro`, the islands, `registry.astro`, `package.json`, and `scripts/docs-data/**` on the candidate stay byte-unchanged.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-SUITE-1: Repair the pre-existing suite breaks on trunk

## What this does

Repairs the seven pre-existing test-suite breaks on trunk — each planner-verified failing on trunk `ca759bd7` independent of any reporting task — so ORI-CI-003/ORI-CI-004's aggregate `pnpm test` acceptance can pass and the shared search-selector class stops failing the Playwright lane. Every repair lives in the seven named test files plus one task-owned proof harness (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/suite-repair-proof.test.ts`) that verifies each named selection now passes; NO product source changes.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-SUITE-1: Repair the pre-existing suite breaks on trunk

## What this does

Repairs the seven pre-existing test-suite breaks on trunk — each planner-verified failing on trunk `ca759bd7` independent of any reporting task — so ORI-CI-003/ORI-CI-004's aggregate `pnpm test` acceptance can pass and the shared search-selector class stops failing the Playwright lane. Every repair lives in the seven named test files plus one task-owned proof harness (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/suite-repair-proof.test.ts`) that verifies each named selection now passes; NO product source changes.

The seven verified breaks and their repairs:

1. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/single-tutorial-gate.test.ts` — 3 pass / 2 fail (`ORI-CI-001-duplicate` at :461, `ORI-CI-001-noncanonical` at :496). Since ORI-CI-002's ordered chain, `check:snippets` runs before Astro's tutorial gate, and the drill's copied/renamed Quickstart carries four source-bound blocks with no committed binding, so the build stops at `[authored-snippets] no committed binding (unbound source-bound block): document apps/docs/src/content/docs/ori-ci-001-second-tutorial.mdx …` before `[docs-data] single-tutorial` can speak — the unpublished draft variant trips it too. Repair: the drill's `runDuplicateCases`/`runNoncanonicalCase` extend (duplicate) or re-point (noncanonical) the SCRATCH copy's `COMMITTED_BINDINGS` in `scripts/docs-data/authored-snippets.ts` for the copy's four source-bound blocks — exactly ORI-CI-002's duplicate-tutorial insertion pattern (`docs-build-pipeline.test.ts` `planDuplicateTutorial`) — restored byte-exactly in the drill's finally. The noncanonical rename must RE-POINT the four quickstart entries (not just add): the stale-binding check at `authored-snippets.ts:945` (`stale binding: … matches no authored block and no emitted element`) rejects the orphaned quickstart bindings once the file is renamed.
2. `tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/scaffold.build.test.ts` — 1 pass / 1 fail (`FUSE-01-manifest-contract` at :142: `dependency "github-slugger" is outside the TR-06 allowed set`; `wrangler` is the next offender behind it; then :162-163 pins the retired three-segment build script). Repair: extend the TR-06 allowed set with exactly the two landed dependencies (`github-slugger`, landed by ORI-AST-001 `bf202aac`; `wrangler`, landed by ORI-DEP-001 `57903f51`) with a supersede comment naming both commits, and supersede the build-script pin to the landed seven-stage public-build form (ORI-CI-002's `ci-chain-order` supersede is the pattern; `STAGE_ORDER` in `docs-build-pipeline.test.ts` is the living contract).
3. `tests/sprint-04-generated-reference/data-table-contract.test.ts` — 3 pass / 1 fail (`:58 rows prop is the required readonly cell-matrix`). AST-007's rich-cell form made `rows` optional (`rows?: readonly { text: string; mono?: boolean }[][]`) and moved the loop to `rows?.map(` with the default-slot rich body. Repair: update the `rows:` regex to the optional form, assert the rich-body slot branch alongside, and re-anchor the exactly-1 loop count to `rows?.map(`.
4. `tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/ledger.spec.ts` — failures across its tokens (planner-verified: 112 `rnr-copy-button button` triggers — two labeled engine commands per row since AST-007; strict-mode on the bulk-add `code` pair — the standalone display `<code>` plus the CopyButton island's internal `code`; `td.ledger-type` now renders the stripped category; `td.ledger-verdict` replaced by the Badge in a plain `td`; `table.ledger__table` replaced by `table.data-table` under `.ledger-table__scroll` with `tbody[data-ledger]`; the Docs column now links `/components/{name}` for all 56 rows via `a[data-docs-link]`). Repair: rewrite the selectors to AST-007's landed LedgerTable shape, adopting the living sprint-05 lane precedents (`ledger-presentation.spec.ts`: row-scoped `.badge`, `[data-engine-command="nativewind"] rnr-copy-button`, `a[data-docs-link]`); retire only the assertions superseded by living sprint-05 lanes (the in-page `#row-` docs-href fragment scheme — every row now has a real ORI-AST-008 destination), and keep rewriting everything that still guards real sprint-01 behavior: 56 rows name-for-name against the generated dataset, verdict vocabulary, absolute-URL command regex, clipboard equality, DOM-order, and the no-JS render.
5. `tests/sprint-03-family-browse/verdict-badge-wiring.spec.ts` — 6 pass / 3 fail (token `FAM-005-ledger-badge-wiring` times out in all three projects): same replaced-selector class (`td.ledger-verdict .badge`, `td.ledger-docs a`, the `#row-` docs-href helper, and the per-row copy count now 2 per row). Repair: same selector rewrite; the `id="row-{name}"` anchor assertions stay (the anchors survive on the `tr`).
6. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/not-found-search-recovery.spec.ts` — 6 pass / 3 fail (the two JS-enabled projects' AC tokens at :488/:706): strict-mode violation `locator('[data-search-slot] button') resolved to 2 elements` — VIS-003's `data-search-close` button landed inside the header slot next to the trigger. Repair: the one-line selector fix, scoping to the trigger's specific selector `'[data-search-slot] button.search-dialog__trigger'` — the exact form the living `search-presentation.spec.ts:40` already uses.
7. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/search-contract.spec.ts` — 5 pass / 10 fail (every JS-enabled token — the locked 13-step sequence and AC-1..AC-4 — in chromium-desktop and chromium-mobile fails at the :208 click on the same strict-mode violation; the no-JS project passes). Same one-line class and same repair as member 6: `SEARCH_TRIGGER` becomes `'[data-search-slot] button.search-dialog__trigger'`; nothing else in the spec changes.

Planner-verified trunk observations recorded 2026-09-25 on `ca759bd7`: single-tutorial-gate 3/2, scaffold.build 1/1, data-table-contract 3/1, ledger.spec failing, verdict-badge-wiring 6/3, not-found-search-recovery 6/3, search-contract 5/10 (all via the exact per-suite selectors preserved below).

## Why

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

The following seven preconditions remain unresolved. Environment-variable presence, cached login state, a registered domain, local proof, or planned runner labels do not establish success. - **VP-AI-PACKAGES** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): Verify published metadata and actual installation of ai@7.0.89, @ai-sdk/react@4.0.92, @ai-sdk/openai@4.0.66 and zod@4.6.1 through Expo tooling. The hook/provider packages were absent locally and the proposed hook pin was not retrievable in the specialist session. Require real LanguageModelV4 compatibility and compiler proof. If the pin is unavailable or incompatible, stop for a version decision; do not silently take latest or add API compatibility shims.

- **VP-OPENAI** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): OPENAI_API_KEY presence is not provider proof. Make actual server-side requests to the fixed official OpenAI Responses endpoint using gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 and record sanitized authentication/model/quota/network outcomes. Require real incremental deltas, contextual history, active abort, rejected-model error and successful retry. No alternate provider/model silently substitutes for the selected contract.

- **VP-NATIVE** (`requires_runtime_setup`): Reserve explicit RNR_S05_IOS_UDID and RNR_S05_ANDROID_SERIAL. Boot the selected available Android AVD; adb had no running target in the specialist observations. Verify compatible Expo Go and real native automation. Preserve unrelated booted simulators. Use separate engine consumers/caches and native worktree-local build outputs. Verify actual expo/fetch streaming, structuredClone and text-encoding globals on each running target; missing required runtime support blocks the owning native task.

- **VP-CANONICAL-AUTHORITY** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): Verify actual owning Cloudflare account, active zone, Worker identity, effective permissions, DNS/custom-domain/routes and absence of conflicts or another deployment owner. Cached local OAuth and registration do not prove authority. Use cached OAuth without reading or copying its token; expired/insufficient access requires the account owner's normal restoration.

- **VP-PUBLIC-DNS-TLS** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): rnraielements.com was registered but not resolving in parent preflight. Wait for actual activation, ordinary public DNS and trusted HTTPS serving the corrected real registry. Do not use hosts-file overrides, local URL rewrites, arbitrary preview hosts or disabled certificate validation to satisfy literal CLI installs.

- **VP-HOSTED-RUNNER** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): Provision and verify an eligible exclusive clean/ephemeral macOS ARM64 native runner, its real device/browser/toolchain capabilities and resource reservations. The rnr-s05-native label is proposed, not observed registered. No personal workstation credential cache enters candidate jobs. Without that runner, hosted full native/provider acceptance remains blocked; local proof cannot impersonate GitHub checks.

- **VP-GITHUB-PROTECTION** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): Verify actual required-check names, workflow availability, same-repository dispatch identity, candidate SHA/event SHA equality, environment protection support, independent approval preventing self-approval, runner-group restrictions and artifact access. Validate action full-SHA provenance before use. Fork/unreviewed code must not receive provider credentials or execute on the protected native runner.

### Execution safeguards

Reserve the real backend, Metro, Web, browser, and native resources. Require the candidate's owned preview on port 4321; identify existing listeners and refuse an unowned conflict. Do not kill unrelated processes or fall back to another origin to satisfy the locked gate. Keep the selected provider secret on the trusted server side, never in Metro, installed consumers, browser code, EXPO_PUBLIC values, arguments, or artifacts.

Use the approved ordered registry/gallery/docs-data/snippet/Astro/Pagefind/link build and current-invocation proof matrix. The initial canonical registry must exist before literal CLI installation. Public registry hashes must match the final accepted candidate; a mismatch requires renewed review and fresh proof. The first domain attachment uses the approved attended Wrangler flow; do not overwrite conflicting ownership automatically.

Retain cleanup evidence for owned requests, timers, listeners, processes, device mappings, appearance changes, and reservations on success and failure. # FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1: Pin react-native-web 0.21.2 in both consumer templates so fresh uniwind web exports resolve

## What this does

Changes exactly one dependency entry in each committed consumer template — `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/package.json` and `packages/docs-snippets/uniwind/package.json` — from the drifting range `"react-native-web": "~0.21.0"` to the exact pin `"react-native-web": "0.21.2"`, and proves the pin with a task-owned harness (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts`) that drives the real fresh-install and export path end to end. No product source beyond the two manifests, no lockfile change: the docs-snippets templates are standalone template directories outside the pnpm workspace (no `packages/docs-snippets/package.json`, zero references in `pnpm-lock.yaml`), so the pin changes only what fresh public installs resolve.

Why exact-pin and not a narrower range: `~0.21.2` and every other operator form still resolves `0.21.3` (the tilde family `~0.21.x` spans `>=0.21.x <0.22.0`), so anything but the bare version re-drifts on the next registry publish. Exact pins are already the tree's convention for sensitive native entries in these same manifests (`react: 19.2.3`, `react-native: 0.86.3`, `uniwind: 1.11.0`, `react-native-worklets: 0.10.1`).

## Why

ORI-CONT-004's cycle-1 blocked report (commit `78f88b07`, report saved at `.kb-run-sprint/sprint-05-orient-search/ORI-CONT-004/cycle-1.blocked.json`) proves the sixth Quickstart seed leg (uniwind/web) is deterministically broken by a registry publish that postdates ORI-RN-003's committed green: react-native-web@0.21.3 (published 2026-09-25T15:00Z) resolves from the templates' `~0.21.0` range, and its new InputAccessoryView export dies inside uniwind 1.11.0's incomplete `package.json` exports map — the `./components/*` wildcard maps to `./dist/module/components/web/*.js`, and the uniwind 1.11.0 tarball ships 28 web components there with InputAccessoryView absent — so `expo export --platform web` fails inside every fresh uniwind consumer under `withUniwindConfig` Metro with `Unable to resolve module ./exports/InputAccessoryView`. Planner-verified facts: the registry candidate set for `~0.21.0` is exactly `0.21.0/0.21.1/0.21.2/0.21.3`; uniwind 1.11.0's `dist/module/components/web/` carries no InputAccessoryView file. Reproduced standalone twice by the reporting child; pinning `react-native-web@0.21.2` in the same consumer exported cleanly (exit 0) both times. Five of six seed legs already pass; the flow fails closed on this leg. Both template-owner tasks (ORI-RN-001, ORI-RN-003) are completed, so no pending task owns the manifests; the wave-20 decision authorized exactly this add.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts
pnpm exec vitest run tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts
```

The first command is the exact selector: the task-owned harness runs the real registry-resolution lane, prepares fresh public consumers from the committed templates through the committed recipes (reused read-only from `support/quickstart-consumer.ts`), reads each consumer's resolved react-native-web version from its own `node_modules`, and runs the real `npx expo export --platform web` (reused read-only from `support/quickstart-web.ts`). `--mode red` captures the pre-pin state (resolved `0.21.3`, failing export with the named module error) in `.tmp/FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1/red.json`; the default GREEN mode proves the pinned state (exact `0.21.2`, uniwind and nativewind exports exit 0) in `green.json`. The second command runs the vitest-visible guard suite only — the heavyweight lanes are CLI-gated behind the direct-invocation check, so the aggregate `pnpm test` never spawns a fresh install. `pnpm typecheck` and the scoped Biome command are preserved static gates recorded in `run.json`.

## Scope

Own the two template manifest entries, the task-owned harness, the pin-record evidence README, the bounded `.tmp/FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1/` evidence, and the two install-log side-effect refreshes the reused helper rewrites. Nothing else: no app source, no registry code, no lockfile, no workspace manifest, no flow or planning artifact.

<!-- Template Version: 5.2.0 -->

> Assignee: react-native-reusables-implementer
> Priority: P1 · Points: 2 · Type: FIX

PROGRESS: 0/3 ACs; every TDD_STATE is none. All evidence paths are future outputs.

### OUTCOME

A fresh public install of either committed consumer template resolves react-native-web exactly 0.21.2 and its real `expo export --platform web` exits 0 on both engines; the pre-pin drift (0.21.3 resolving from `~0.21.0` and killing the uniwind export with `Unable to resolve module ./exports/InputAccessoryView`) is captured as functional RED; the harness is aggregate-safe, the static gates pass, and the diff is confined to the two manifest entries plus the harness and its evidence — unblocking ORI-CONT-004's sixth Quickstart seed leg and the per-engine live matrices behind it.

### CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS — Never

- Never widen the fix beyond the pin: no uniwind upgrade or downgrade, no metro.config.js change, no exports-map patching, no lockfile edit. If the exact 0.21.2 pin alone does not make the uniwind export exit 0, stop and report — the root-cause claim is wrong and a scope amendment is required.
- Never pin with a range operator (`~0.21.2`, `^0.21.2`, `>=0.21.2 <0.22.0`): every operator form can resolve 0.21.3 on a future fresh install; the pinned entries must be the bare version string `0.21.2`.
- Never substitute for the real resolution mechanics: no authored registry output where the real `npm view react-native-web@<range> version --json` belongs, no lockfile read where the consumer's own `node_modules/react-native-web/package.json` belongs, no authored export receipt where a real `expo export` exit belongs.
- Never substitute a local registry, hostname rewriting, or monorepo resolution for the public apex (ORI-RN-001's disallowed substitutions); the consumers live outside the monorepo and install from rnraielements.com and the npm registry, exactly as the tutorials display.
- Never trim the consumer to a bare template without the public CLI adds: the failing import graph only exists in the full consumer the recipe builds; a componentless template can export cleanly under 0.21.3 and would fake a RED absence.
- Never let the harness spawn fresh installs from inside a vitest process: the heavyweight lanes run only behind the direct-invocation check (`process.argv[1]` equals the file), and the vitest-visible guard suite is network-free.
- Never edit the workspace manifests (`apps/harness`, `apps/harness-nativewind`, `apps/example`) that carry the same `~0.21.0` range: they resolve through `pnpm-lock.yaml`, not fresh public installs, and are outside this task's boundary — record them as a report-only finding.
- Never touch in-flight surfaces (ORI-CONT-004's spec and evidence, ORI-AI-002's runner), planning artifacts, `human-flows.json`, `gate-plan.json`, or perform trunk/worktree lifecycle operations.

### DONE WHEN

- [ ] AC-1 proves the pre-pin RED (resolved 0.21.3, export exit != 0 with the literal module error) and the post-pin GREEN (exact 0.21.2 in both manifests, resolved 0.21.2, uniwind export exit 0) through one real fresh install per phase.
- [ ] AC-2 proves the nativewind consumer resolves exactly 0.21.2 and still exports cleanly under the pin.
- [ ] AC-3 proves the guard selector, static gates, and the exact write boundary (0 paths outside the allowlist, 0 lockfile changes, 0 range operators in the pinned entries).
- [ ] The exact selectors and preserved commands pass; independent review confirms functional RED, seeded evidence, and no stubs.

### SPECIFICATION

One-line exact pin in each of the two template manifests, plus a task-owned proof harness that reuses the ORI-RN-001/ORI-RN-003 support modules read-only. The harness is the sibling FIX shape: a CLI-gated `main()` (default GREEN mode, `--mode red` for the RED capture), an exported `runRnwPinProof` proof entry, and a vitest-visible network-free guard suite so the file contributes a passing test — not a No-test-suite failure — to the aggregate run.

### BOUNDARY CONTRACTS

1. The pin: `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/package.json` and `packages/docs-snippets/uniwind/package.json` each change exactly the react-native-web dependency entry to the bare string `0.21.2`. No other key, file formatting beyond that line, or sibling manifest changes.
2. Harness `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts` (NEW): lane A — real registry resolution (`npm view react-native-web@<committed-range> version --json`), asserting the candidate set for the committed form (RED: contains `0.21.3`; GREEN: exactly `['0.21.2']`); lane B — fresh consumer per engine via the reused `prepareConsumer` (the committed recipe verbatim: `pnpm install`, `npx expo install`, the literal public CLI adds, `tsc --noEmit`, `expo-doctor`), reading the resolved version from the consumer's `node_modules/react-native-web/package.json`; lane C — the reused `exportWeb` (real `npx expo export --platform web --output-dir <scratch>`), asserting exit and log literals. RED mode runs lanes A–C for uniwind against the pre-pin manifests and writes `red.json`; GREEN mode runs A for the exact pin, B–C for both engines, asserts the pinned manifest form (bare `0.21.2`, 0 range operators), and writes `green.json`; both modes merge command/exit/run-identity bindings into `run.json`. Env hygiene at entry: delete `NODE_ENV`, use a short reaper-free `TMPDIR` for the consumer roots; overall GREEN budget <= 90 min, recorded. Cleanup: remove the tmpdir consumer roots on every exit path; keep the scratch dist dirs referenced in evidence until teardown.
3. Guard suite: a vitest-visible `describe`/`it` pair asserting the committed manifests' react-native-web entry is exactly `0.21.2` and that the heavyweight lanes are gated behind the direct-invocation check — no network, no spawns; it fails pre-pin (honest RED in the aggregate) and passes post-pin.
4. Side effects: the reused `prepareConsumer` rewrites `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-RN-001/nativewind-install.txt` and `uniwind-install.txt` in place; those refreshes are write-allowed, committed with the run, never hand-edited or deleted. The harness's own evidence lands in `.tmp/FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1/` and `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1/README.md` (the pin record: root cause, the registry candidate set, both engines' resolved versions and export exits, and the citation of the reporting child's two standalone 0.21.2 verifications).

### ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — RED → GREEN → REFACTOR

Only AC-1 is PRIMARY. All criteria run the real install and export path on the real stack.

#### AC-1: The exact 0.21.2 pin makes a fresh uniwind consumer resolve it and export cleanly [PRIMARY]

GIVEN the two committed consumer templates and the task-owned harness WHEN the harness prepares a fresh public uniwind consumer from the committed template through the real committed recipe and runs the real `npx expo export --platform web` THEN pre-pin the consumer resolves react-native-web exactly '0.21.3' and the export exits != 0 with the literal 'Unable to resolve module ./exports/InputAccessoryView', and post-pin both manifests declare the exact pin (0 range operators) and an identical fresh consumer resolves exactly '0.21.2' with the export exiting 0.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

The following seven preconditions remain unresolved. Environment-variable presence, cached login state, a registered domain, local proof, or planned runner labels do not establish success. - **VP-AI-PACKAGES** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): Verify published metadata and actual installation of ai@7.0.89, @ai-sdk/react@4.0.92, @ai-sdk/openai@4.0.66 and zod@4.6.1 through Expo tooling. If the pin is unavailable or incompatible, stop for a version decision; do not silently take latest or add API compatibility shims.

Boot the selected available Android AVD; adb had no running target in the specialist observations. Verify compatible Expo Go and real native automation. Preserve unrelated booted simulators. Verify actual expo/fetch streaming, structuredClone and text-encoding globals on each running target; missing required runtime support blocks the owning native task.

- **VP-CANONICAL-AUTHORITY** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): Verify actual owning Cloudflare account, active zone, Worker identity, effective permissions, DNS/custom-domain/routes and absence of conflicts or another deployment owner. Cached local OAuth and registration do not prove authority. Use cached OAuth without reading or copying its token; expired/insufficient access requires the account owner's normal restoration.

- **VP-PUBLIC-DNS-TLS** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): rnraielements.com was registered but not resolving in parent preflight. Wait for actual activation, ordinary public DNS and trusted HTTPS serving the corrected real registry. Do not use hosts-file overrides, local URL rewrites, arbitrary preview hosts or disabled certificate validation to satisfy literal CLI installs.

- **VP-HOSTED-RUNNER** (`unverified_external_prerequisite`): Provision and verify an eligible exclusive clean/ephemeral macOS ARM64 native runner, its real device/browser/toolchain capabilities and resource reservations. The rnr-s05-native label is proposed, not observed registered. No personal workstation credential cache enters candidate jobs. Without that runner, hosted full native/provider acceptance remains blocked; local proof cannot impersonate GitHub checks.

### Execution safeguards

Reserve the real backend, Metro, Web, browser, and native resources. Require the candidate's owned preview on port 4321; identify existing listeners and refuse an unowned conflict. Do not kill unrelated processes or fall back to another origin to satisfy the locked gate. Keep the selected provider secret on the trusted server side, never in Metro, installed consumers, browser code, EXPO_PUBLIC values, arguments, or artifacts.

Use the approved ordered registry/gallery/docs-data/snippet/Astro/Pagefind/link build and current-invocation proof matrix. The initial canonical registry must exist before literal CLI installation. The first domain attachment uses the approved attended Wrangler flow; do not overwrite conflicting ownership automatically.

# FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1: Pin react-native-web 0.21.2 in both consumer templates so fresh uniwind web exports resolve

## What this does

Changes exactly one dependency entry in each committed consumer template — `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/package.json` and `packages/docs-snippets/uniwind/package.json` — from the drifting range `"react-native-web": "~0.21.0"` to the exact pin `"react-native-web": "0.21.2"`, and proves the pin with a task-owned harness (`tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts`) that drives the real fresh-install and export path end to end. No product source beyond the two manifests, no lockfile change: the docs-snippets templates are standalone template directories outside the pnpm workspace (no `packages/docs-snippets/package.json`, zero references in `pnpm-lock.yaml`), so the pin changes only what fresh public installs resolve.

Why exact-pin and not a narrower range: `~0.21.2` and every other operator form still resolves `0.21.3` (the tilde family `~0.21.x` spans `>=0.21.x <0.22.0`), so anything but the bare version re-drifts on the next registry publish. Exact pins are already the tree's convention for sensitive native entries in these same manifests (`react: 19.2.3`, `react-native: 0.86.3`, `uniwind: 1.11.0`, `react-native-worklets: 0.10.1`).

## Why

ORI-CONT-004's cycle-1 blocked report (commit `78f88b07`, report saved at `.kb-run-sprint/sprint-05-orient-search/ORI-CONT-004/cycle-1.blocked.json`) proves the sixth Quickstart seed leg (uniwind/web) is deterministically broken by a registry publish that postdates ORI-RN-003's committed green: react-native-web@0.21.3 (published 2026-09-25T15:00Z) resolves from the templates' `~0.21.0` range, and its new InputAccessoryView export dies inside uniwind 1.11.0's incomplete `package.json` exports map — the `./components/*` wildcard maps to `./dist/module/components/web/*.js`, and the uniwind 1.11.0 tarball ships 28 web components there with InputAccessoryView absent — so `expo export --platform web` fails inside every fresh uniwind consumer under `withUniwindConfig` Metro with `Unable to resolve module ./exports/InputAccessoryView`. Planner-verified facts: the registry candidate set for `~0.21.0` is exactly `0.21.0/0.21.1/0.21.2/0.21.3`; uniwind 1.11.0's `dist/module/components/web/` carries no InputAccessoryView file. Reproduced standalone twice by the reporting child; pinning `react-native-web@0.21.2` in the same consumer exported cleanly (exit 0) both times. Five of six seed legs already pass; the flow fails closed on this leg. Both template-owner tasks (ORI-RN-001, ORI-RN-003) are completed, so no pending task owns the manifests; the wave-20 decision authorized exactly this add.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts
pnpm exec vitest run tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts
```

The first command is the exact selector: the task-owned harness runs the real registry-resolution lane, prepares fresh public consumers from the committed templates through the committed recipes (reused read-only from `support/quickstart-consumer.ts`), reads each consumer's resolved react-native-web version from its own `node_modules`, and runs the real `npx expo export --platform web` (reused read-only from `support/quickstart-web.ts`). `--mode red` captures the pre-pin state (resolved `0.21.3`, failing export with the named module error) in `.tmp/FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1/red.json`; the default GREEN mode proves the pinned state (exact `0.21.2`, uniwind and nativewind exports exit 0) in `green.json`. The second command runs the vitest-visible guard suite only — the heavyweight lanes are CLI-gated behind the direct-invocation check, so the aggregate `pnpm test` never spawns a fresh install. `pnpm typecheck` and the scoped Biome command are preserved static gates recorded in `run.json`.

## Scope

Own the two template manifest entries, the task-owned harness, the pin-record evidence README, the bounded `.tmp/FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1/` evidence, and the two install-log side-effect refreshes the reused helper rewrites. Nothing else: no app source, no registry code, no lockfile, no workspace manifest, no flow or planning artifact.

### OUTCOME

A fresh public install of either committed consumer template resolves react-native-web exactly 0.21.2 and its real `expo export --platform web` exits 0 on both engines; the pre-pin drift (0.21.3 resolving from `~0.21.0` and killing the uniwind export with `Unable to resolve module ./exports/InputAccessoryView`) is captured as functional RED; the harness is aggregate-safe, the static gates pass, and the diff is confined to the two manifest entries plus the harness and its evidence — unblocking ORI-CONT-004's sixth Quickstart seed leg and the per-engine live matrices behind it.

### CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS — Never

- Never widen the fix beyond the pin: no uniwind upgrade or downgrade, no metro.config.js change, no exports-map patching, no lockfile edit. If the exact 0.21.2 pin alone does not make the uniwind export exit 0, stop and report — the root-cause claim is wrong and a scope amendment is required.
- Never pin with a range operator (`~0.21.2`, `^0.21.2`, `>=0.21.2 <0.22.0`): every operator form can resolve 0.21.3 on a future fresh install; the pinned entries must be the bare version string `0.21.2`.
- Never substitute for the real resolution mechanics: no authored registry output where the real `npm view react-native-web@<range> version --json` belongs, no lockfile read where the consumer's own `node_modules/react-native-web/package.json` belongs, no authored export receipt where a real `expo export` exit belongs.
- Never substitute a local registry, hostname rewriting, or monorepo resolution for the public apex (ORI-RN-001's disallowed substitutions); the consumers live outside the monorepo and install from rnraielements.com and the npm registry, exactly as the tutorials display.
- Never trim the consumer to a bare template without the public CLI adds: the failing import graph only exists in the full consumer the recipe builds; a componentless template can export cleanly under 0.21.3 and would fake a RED absence.
- Never let the harness spawn fresh installs from inside a vitest process: the heavyweight lanes run only behind the direct-invocation check (`process.argv[1]` equals the file), and the vitest-visible guard suite is network-free.
- Never edit the workspace manifests (`apps/harness`, `apps/harness-nativewind`, `apps/example`) that carry the same `~0.21.0` range: they resolve through `pnpm-lock.yaml`, not fresh public installs, and are outside this task's boundary — record them as a report-only finding.
- Never touch in-flight surfaces (ORI-CONT-004's spec and evidence, ORI-AI-002's runner), planning artifacts, `human-flows.json`, `gate-plan.json`, or perform trunk/worktree lifecycle operations.

### DONE WHEN

- [ ] AC-1 proves the pre-pin RED (resolved 0.21.3, export exit != 0 with the literal module error) and the post-pin GREEN (exact 0.21.2 in both manifests, resolved 0.21.2, uniwind export exit 0) through one real fresh install per phase.
- [ ] AC-2 proves the nativewind consumer resolves exactly 0.21.2 and still exports cleanly under the pin.
- [ ] AC-3 proves the guard selector, static gates, and the exact write boundary (0 paths outside the allowlist, 0 lockfile changes, 0 range operators in the pinned entries).
- [ ] The exact selectors and preserved commands pass; independent review confirms functional RED, seeded evidence, and no stubs.

### SPECIFICATION

One-line exact pin in each of the two template manifests, plus a task-owned proof harness that reuses the ORI-RN-001/ORI-RN-003 support modules read-only. The harness is the sibling FIX shape: a CLI-gated `main()` (default GREEN mode, `--mode red` for the RED capture), an exported `runRnwPinProof` proof entry, and a vitest-visible network-free guard suite so the file contributes a passing test — not a No-test-suite failure — to the aggregate run.

### BOUNDARY CONTRACTS

1. The pin: `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/package.json` and `packages/docs-snippets/uniwind/package.json` each change exactly the react-native-web dependency entry to the bare string `0.21.2`. No other key, file formatting beyond that line, or sibling manifest changes.
2. Harness `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/rnw-pin-proof.test.ts` (NEW): lane A — real registry resolution (`npm view react-native-web@<committed-range> version --json`), asserting the candidate set for the committed form (RED: contains `0.21.3`; GREEN: exactly `['0.21.2']`); lane B — fresh consumer per engine via the reused `prepareConsumer` (the committed recipe verbatim: `pnpm install`, `npx expo install`, the literal public CLI adds, `tsc --noEmit`, `expo-doctor`), reading the resolved version from the consumer's `node_modules/react-native-web/package.json`; lane C — the reused `exportWeb` (real `npx expo export --platform web --output-dir <scratch>`), asserting exit and log literals. RED mode runs lanes A–C for uniwind against the pre-pin manifests and writes `red.json`; GREEN mode runs A for the exact pin, B–C for both engines, asserts the pinned manifest form (bare `0.21.2`, 0 range operators), and writes `green.json`; both modes merge command/exit/run-identity bindings into `run.json`. Env hygiene at entry: delete `NODE_ENV`, use a short reaper-free `TMPDIR` for the consumer roots; overall GREEN budget <= 90 min, recorded. Cleanup: remove the tmpdir consumer roots on every exit path; keep the scratch dist dirs referenced in evidence until teardown.
3. Guard suite: a vitest-visible `describe`/`it` pair asserting the committed manifests' react-native-web entry is exactly `0.21.2` and that the heavyweight lanes are gated behind the direct-invocation check — no network, no spawns; it fails pre-pin (honest RED in the aggregate) and passes post-pin.
4. Side effects: the reused `prepareConsumer` rewrites `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-RN-001/nativewind-install.txt` and `uniwind-install.txt` in place; those refreshes are write-allowed, committed with the run, never hand-edited or deleted. The harness's own evidence lands in `.tmp/FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1/` and `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/FIX-ORI-CONT-004-1/README.md` (the pin record: root cause, the registry candidate set, both engines' resolved versions and export exits, and the citation of the reporting child's two standalone 0.21.2 verifications).

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-SUITE-2: Repair the foreign suite drifts behind the aggregate's residual failures

## What this does

Repairs the foreign test-suite failures that keep the aggregate `pnpm test` red after the seven-suite repair — each planner-verified STANDALONE on the recorded candidate (`2f15ba41`, byte-identical to trunk `dbf3c0af` for every suite file this task may touch) — and honestly routes the two reported failures that are NOT test drift. Four foreign suites carry real test-side drift or runtime-class damage; the other two of the six reported failures are owner-routed or environmental, and this task does NOT charter a mask for either.

The planner-verified per-suite ledger (every observation below was reproduced by the planner on `2f15ba41` via the exact per-suite selectors preserved in this charter):

1. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/docs-collection.test.ts` (ORI-AST-001) — 2 of 4 tokens verified failing FAST (`ORI-AST-001-collection-schema` and `ORI-AST-001-publication-contract` each die at the first scratch build: `'valid build exits 0': expected 1 to be +0` inside ~1.5 s; `ORI-AST-001-mdx-code-copy` was reported failing in the same window and needs the same fixture repair plus a free 4321 for Part A; `ORI-AST-001-prose-navigation` passes). ROOT CAUSE verified by scratch reproduction: `makeScratch()` (docs-collection.test.ts:92-108) mirrors only the root `package.json` plus `apps/docs/**`, but the landed app now references two more repo-root trees — `apps/docs/src/components/TokenTable.astro:5` imports `../../../../scripts/docs-data/token-map` (landed by ORI-AST-003), and the quickstart page's render-time source read opens `packages/docs-snippets/shared/quickstart-messages.ts` (the ORI-CONT-003/FIX-ORI-CI-001-1 tutorial designation), so every scratch build dies `UNRESOLVED_IMPORT` (scripts absent) and then `ENOENT ... quickstart-messages.ts` (render-time). VERIFIED REPAIR: with exactly `scripts/` and `packages/docs-snippets/` mirrored into the scratch, the identical scratch `astro build` exits 0 with `Complete!` and emits `dist/docs/collection-reference/index.html`. The repair is the fixture: extend `makeScratch()` to mirror the two root trees, exactly the existing root-`package.json` precedent at docs-collection.test.ts:95.
2. `tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/docs-data-prebuild.test.ts` (FUSE-05) — the full file verified standalone: 1 failed / 3 passed (~11 min; both 900-second build drills pass). The sole failure is `copies public r generated-only and byte-identical` at :323 — `git ls-files apps/docs/public` must be empty, but ORI-VIS-001 (`1c732dc1`) landed five AUTHORED font files under `apps/docs/public/fonts/` (`OFL.txt`, `spline-sans-mono-var-latin-ext.woff2`, `spline-sans-mono-var-latin.woff2`, `spline-sans-var-latin-ext.woff2`, `spline-sans-var-latin.woff2`). The 57-per-engine counts, the byte-identity mirror, and every check-ignore assertion above :323 pass unchanged. Repair: scope the tracked-files assertion to the GENERATED subtree — `git ls-files apps/docs/public/r` must be empty — with a supersede comment naming `1c732dc1`; the authored fonts stay tracked by design.
3. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/live-example-api.test.ts` (FLOW-DOCS-02) — token `AC-4 pins the hook contract, compiles both graphs and tears down owned children` verified failing standalone at :631 — `expect(hookSource).toContain("from 'expo/fetch'")` is stale since FIX-ORI-AI-001-1 (`755edeae`) moved the hook to the lazy form `const { fetch: expoFetch } = await import('expo/fetch')` at `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts:46` (the lazy import lets the module load outside Metro). Everything else in the token verified current on the candidate: both `tsc --noEmit` compiles exit 0 (`apps/example/server/tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.live-chat.json`), all four PINS read back exactly (`ai@7.0.89`, `@ai-sdk/react@4.0.92`, `@ai-sdk/openai@4.0.66`, `zod@4.6.1`), and every other hook literal is present (`DefaultChatTransport`, `throttle: 50`, `messages: []` at use-live-chat.ts:203, `clearError();` before `regenerate();` at :20-21). Repair: the one literal takes the current lazy form; every neighboring oracle stays byte-effective.
4. `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/nativewind-live-example.test.ts` (ORI-RN-005) — the two marathon tokens (`ORI-RN-005-abort-error-retry` :201, `ORI-RN-005-fail-closed-cleanup` :270, both `timeout: 75 * 60_000`) failed inside the 16-hour aggregate. The recorded run manifests (`.tmp/ORI-RN-005/{abort-error-retry,fail-closed-cleanup}/manifest.json`) show CONCLUDED runs (`teardown.json` written with fresh `finished_at` — 2026-09-26T05:30:49Z and 09:35:21Z) whose legs failed on runtime observations, not assertion drift: iOS `seed turn ended as no terminal record`, Android `"Live chat" never appeared (60s)`, web `growthSamples: []`. The 5-entry source manifest (`nativewind-live-source-manifest.json`) verified hash-current against every mapped source — no drift. RUNTIME CLASS: this task stands both tokens back up STANDALONE in a reserved-device quiet window (real iOS simulator, Android emulator, web export, owned backend, official OpenAI Responses endpoint), and may adjust the per-token budget ONLY on observed timeout-mechanism evidence with the kill-retry arithmetic recorded (`runDriverWithKillRetry` :93-111 doubles any externally-killed run — a 30-35 min full run retried once exceeds nothing at 75 min, but a fail-closed case-3 full run plus a retried leg can; the math must be in the comment and the handoff). A leg failure that reproduces standalone for a PRODUCT reason is a blocked report owner-routed to the ORI-RN-005 surface — never a mask, never a skip, never a lowered assertion.

Owner-routed — NOT chartered for repair: `tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/ci-chain-order.test.ts` (FLOW-DELIV-01). Planner-verified: its FUSE-12 lane AC-1 (the `... ships 112 dist JSONs` token — the 114 current-literal already landed at :246-248 with 57-per-engine at :255) PASSES standalone, and AC-2 (the ci.yml parse proof) PASSES standalone. The suite's only failing token is `FLOW-DELIV-01-ci-chain-order` (:66), which runs the root `pnpm e2e:docs` twice — the full Playwright lane — whose only currently-failing spec token is `recovery-presentation.spec.ts` ac-5 (:745-806): the public-origin prerequisite that hard-throws `PUBLIC PREREQUISITE unmet` until ORI-DEP-002/003 publish the reviewed candidate at the apex (planner probe 2026-09-26: `https://rnraielements.com/<unknown-path>` answers HTTP 404 with an EMPTY body — no branded recovery surface). No test edit can make that token pass before deployment; the file stays outside this task's boundary. The stale `'[data-search-slot] button'` constant at `recovery-presentation.spec.ts:52` is LATENT only — its two uses (:522, :611) are `toBeHidden()` assertions, which are strict-mode-exempt and pass with the close button present — so no repair is chartered there either; report-only.

Environmental — NOT chartered as an assertion change: `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/contributing-content.test.ts` (ORI-CONT-006). Planner-verified 4/4 PASS standalone on the candidate (the `ORI-CONT-006-real-docs-checks` token runs the real build / check:snippets / check:links chain green). Its aggregate failure was the end-of-run tmpdir-reaper cascade that killed 87 collections (~/.cache/agent-scratch vite transform scratch reaped ~16 h in). The remedy this task owns is RUN HYGIENE for the one aggregate rerun: a stable TMPDIR outside the agent-session scratch, recorded in run.json — no edit to the suite.

AGGREGATE REALITY this charter encodes honestly: the vitest aggregate includes ci-chain-order's full-e2e token, so `pnpm test` cannot exit 0 before ORI-DEP-002/003 publish the candidate at the public origin. AC-3 therefore defines an attributed-residual gate: the aggregate is run ONCE (never harness-spawned), its complete failing inventory is recorded, and every suite outside a named residual closure must be green in-aggregate. Nothing residual is silent.

## Why

The in-flight seven-suite repair landed all seven chartered repairs and proved them green in isolation, then blocked honestly on its aggregate clause: six foreign suites fail on the candidate through no fault of those repairs (cycle-1 blocked report, recorded 2026-09-26; wave-21 decision). This task owns the four of those six that are test-side drift or runtime-class damage — each planner-verified standalone in this planning pass, with the two non-drift failures routed to their owners instead of masked — so the aggregate's residual failure set collapses to exactly the deployment-gated closure that ORI-DEP-002/003 own. The owning tasks of the drifted suites (ORI-AST-001, FUSE-05/FLOW-DELIV-01, ORI-AI-001, ORI-RN-005, ORI-CONT-006) are all completed; the drift is collateral of landed, reviewed sprint-05 work (ORI-AST-003's token-map import, ORI-CONT-003/FIX-ORI-CI-001-1's render-time snippet read, ORI-VIS-001's authored fonts, FIX-ORI-AI-001-1's lazy expo/fetch import) and of the 16-hour serialized aggregate environment.

## How to verify

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run tests/sprint-05-orient-search/foreign-suite-repair-proof.test.ts
pnpm test
pnpm typecheck
pnpm exec biome ci tests/sprint-05-orient-search/docs-collection.test.ts tests/sprint-01-docs-spike-skeleton/docs-data-prebuild.test.ts tests/sprint-05-orient-search/live-example-api.test.ts tests/sprint-05-orient-search/nativewind-live-example.test.ts tests/sprint-05-orient-search/foreign-suite-repair-proof.test.ts
```

The first command is the exact selector: the task-owned proof harness spawns each named per-suite selector (the three drifted vitest suites, the live-example-api AC-4 token, and the two NativeWind marathon tokens with per-child timeouts sized to their real envelopes), asserts exit 0 for each, runs `pnpm typecheck` and the scoped Biome command, and asserts the tracked-file diff boundary — recording RED (the planner-verified standalone failures above, bound to the pre-change candidate SHA) and GREEN (per-selector exit 0) in `.tmp/FIX-ORI-SUITE-2/`. `pnpm test` (the aggregate vitest run), `pnpm typecheck`, and the scoped Biome command are preserved GREEN commands the implementer runs and records in `run.json`; the harness never spawns the aggregate (a vitest child spawning the vitest aggregate would re-run every drill and the harness — unbounded recursion).

## Scope

Own exactly the four named test files, the task-owned proof harness, drill-emitted evidence writes, and bounded `.tmp/FIX-ORI-SUITE-2/` evidence. Zero product-source changes: the docs-collection fixture repair COPIES `scripts/` and `packages/docs-snippets/` into its owned scratch and never edits the originals; `apps/**`, `packages/**`, and `scripts/**` on the candidate stay byte-unchanged. The two non-drift failures stay outside the boundary: ci-chain-order.test.ts and recovery-presentation.spec.ts are owner-routed to ORI-DEP-002/003 (report-only), and contributing-content.test.ts is verified green standalone (run-hygiene only, no edit).

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. ## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.
