# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-AI-001-1: Keep the worked example hook's regenerate payload itemIds unique

## What this does

Fixes the worked example's retry defect at its root. After owned-endpoint loss, the `useLiveChat` hook's clearError-then-regenerate path assembles an outgoing payload containing duplicated assistant message entries that carry repeated OpenAI itemIds in `providerMetadata`; the real OpenAI Responses endpoint rejects that payload and the server emits an error record with 0 deltas. The fix keeps every assistant provider-metadata itemId unique across the outgoing history before the transport serializes the request body.

## Why

ORI-RN-004's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint a86231aa) root-caused the iOS/Android retry-completion failure headlessly with the hook's exact SDK classes (`Chat` from @ai-sdk/react 4.0.92 + `DefaultChatTransport` from ai 7.0.89, throttle 50) and bisected it on the real backend: any payload variant leaving each itemId unique completes. Web passes only because its fresh-session path never regenerates with stale history. No pending task owns the hook file — ORI-RN-004's write-allowlist cannot reach `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, and ORI-AI-001 is completed — while the gate's locked steps already promise retry completion. The missing piece is this hook-side fix.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/live-chat-regenerate-payload.test.ts` against the real owned backend and the official OpenAI Responses endpoint. The driver imports the real `Chat` + `DefaultChatTransport` classes from apps/example's installed packages, reproduces the endpoint-loss retry state through the owned backend lifecycle, captures the outgoing bodies and the server's sanitized records, and proves functional RED before the fix and GREEN after. Also run the preserved scoped compiler command below.

## Scope

Own the regenerate-payload fix in `apps/example/lib/use-live-chat.ts`, one new scoped driver under `tests/sprint-05-orient-search/support/`, and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-AI-001-1/`. Rendered retry acceptance on devices remains with ORI-RN-004; the server, the screen and the native drivers stay untouched.

### CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS — Never

- Never expose OPENAI_API_KEY to client imports, EXPO_PUBLIC variables, install/compiler processes, command arguments or captured evidence. Credentials reach only the trusted launcher and the server child.
- Never mock the thing under test: no mocked Chat, transport, fetch, server or provider. Drive the REAL classes installed for apps/example (ai@7.0.89, @ai-sdk/react@4.0.92) against the REAL backend route and the REAL OpenAI Responses endpoint.
- Never satisfy retry by duplicating the user turn (re-sending via sendMessage), swallowing the error, retrying silently in a loop, or classifying an errored HTTP 200 stream as completed.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-RN-005-1: Make the canonical live-chat sources compile in the independent NativeWind consumer

## What this does

Fixes the two compile defects that block ORI-RN-005's clean-consumer proof. In the prescribed independent NativeWind consumer — fresh Expo 57 root outside the monorepo from ORI-RN-001's committed template, registry items from the literal public recipe, the verified hook pins, and the five canonical app sources copied byte-identical — the consumer's own `tsc --noEmit` rejects with exactly two errors, both in landed files outside ORI-RN-005's write scope:

1. `apps/example/components/live-chat-screen.tsx:5` — `import { useUniwind } from 'uniwind'` → TS2307 in a consumer that never adds uniwind. The hook's only use is `theme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light'` feeding `THEME[mode].background`; the behavior-preserving fix is React Native's `useColorScheme`.
2. `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts:8` — `const THEME` is not exported while the canonical screen imports `{ THEME } from '@/lib/theme'` (apps/example's own lib/theme.ts exports it) → TS2459. One-word fix: `export const THEME`.

## Why

ORI-RN-005's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint 20f4b6a6) proved everything else green and root-caused the failure to exactly these two errors. No pending task can fix them: ORI-RN-005's write allowlist excludes `apps/example/**` and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/**` except its package.json; ORI-RN-001, ORI-RN-004 and ORI-AI-001 are completed. Behavior preservation is grounded in the landed code: apps/example's only theme control (`apps/example/gallery/chrome.tsx`) flips the app via `Appearance.setColorScheme` — exactly the signal `useColorScheme()` tracks — and the NativeWind consumer root (`packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/app/_layout.tsx`) already themes via `useColorScheme()`. After this lands, ORI-RN-005 reruns its blocked legs with no further work in its own files.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx .tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-005-1/consumer-compile-proof.ts` — the task-owned scratch harness that materializes the prescribed consumer, copies the five canonical sources byte-identical (SHA-256 pairs), runs the consumer's `tsc --noEmit` (functional RED pre-fix with exactly the two named errors, GREEN post-fix), and records the preserved repository checks. Also run the preserved commands below.

## Scope

Own the two one-line fixes in `apps/example/components/live-chat-screen.tsx` and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts`, plus the scratch harness and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-005-1/`. On-device behavior remains ORI-RN-005's rerun and ORI-AI-002's matrix; every ORI-RN-005 in-flight file stays untouched.

<summary>▸ Full agent specification (TASK-TEMPLATE v5.2 — required reading for implementer + reviewer)</summary>

PROGRESS: 0/2 ACs; every TDD_STATE is none. All evidence paths are future outputs.

### OUTCOME

The five canonical app sources compile clean (`tsc --noEmit` exit 0, expo-doctor exit 0) in the prescribed independent NativeWind consumer, with the canonical screen's theme read engine-agnostic and the template's `THEME` exported; both owning apps' public behavior, exports and compile surfaces are unchanged.

### CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS — Never

- Never weaken the consumer oracle: fresh consumer outside the monorepo, literal public recipe over real HTTPS, five byte-identical copies with SHA-256 pair validation, the consumer's own `tsc`. No declaration shims, no monorepo-resolved imports, no skipLibCheck/path-rewrite concealment, no filtering errors from output.
- Never remove or rename public API: `THEME`'s export is additive; `NAV_THEME`, every token value, and the screen's rendered structure and accessibility labels stay unchanged.
- Never change the theme mapping semantics: dark ⇔ scheme 'dark', everything else (including null) → 'light', exactly as before.
- Never leave the canonical screen importing uniwind or introduce uniwind anywhere in the NativeWind path (engine mixing).
- Never touch ORI-RN-005's in-flight files (its driver, manifest, test, evidence, and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/package.json`); never edit the other four canonical sources.
- Never change pinned versions or the lockfile to force green; never write outside the exact allowlist.

### DONE WHEN

- [ ] AC-1 proves the screen fix: the TS2307 uniwind error is gone from the consumer compile and the Uniwind-app compile surface stays green with identical dark/light behavior.
- [ ] AC-2 proves the THEME export: the TS2459 error is gone, the export is additive-only, and the root compile/lint surfaces stay green.
- [ ] The exact selector and preserved commands pass; independent review confirms functional RED, seeded evidence and no stubs.

### SPECIFICATION

Two one-line root-cause fixes plus a scratch compile harness. The harness reproduces ORI-RN-005's consumer shape at this task's dependency position (its driver and manifest exist only on its parked branch and must not become dependencies): ORI-RN-001's committed template files and literal recipe, the ORI-AI-001-proven hook pins installed through Expo's resolver in the scratch consumer, the five canonical copies, then the consumer's own compiler.

### BOUNDARY CONTRACTS

1. Screen fix: remove `import { useUniwind } from 'uniwind'`; import `useColorScheme` from `react-native`; `const { theme } = useUniwind()` → `const colorScheme = useColorScheme()`; keep `const mode = colorScheme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light'`; update only the stale narrowing comment. Nothing else changes.
2. Theme fix: `const THEME = {` → `export const THEME = {` in `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts`; every value, `NAV_THEME` and the comments otherwise byte-identical. The uniwind template's `lib/theme.ts` is NOT in scope — grep in-task to confirm no canonical source compiled in a uniwind consumer imports `THEME` from the template (apps/example resolves `@/lib/theme` to its own exporting copy; ORI-RN-002's seed screen does not import it); if that changes, separate ask.

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

# FIX-ORI-RN-005-1: Make the canonical live-chat sources compile in the independent NativeWind consumer

## What this does

Fixes the two compile defects that block ORI-RN-005's clean-consumer proof. In the prescribed independent NativeWind consumer — fresh Expo 57 root outside the monorepo from ORI-RN-001's committed template, registry items from the literal public recipe, the verified hook pins, and the five canonical app sources copied byte-identical — the consumer's own `tsc --noEmit` rejects with exactly two errors, both in landed files outside ORI-RN-005's write scope:

1. `apps/example/components/live-chat-screen.tsx:5` — `import { useUniwind } from 'uniwind'` → TS2307 in a consumer that never adds uniwind. The hook's only use is `theme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'light'` feeding `THEME[mode].background`; the behavior-preserving fix is React Native's `useColorScheme`.
2. `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts:8` — `const THEME` is not exported while the canonical screen imports `{ THEME } from '@/lib/theme'` (apps/example's own lib/theme.ts exports it) → TS2459. One-word fix: `export const THEME`.

## Why

ORI-RN-005's cycle-1 blocked report (checkpoint 20f4b6a6) proved everything else green and root-caused the failure to exactly these two errors. No pending task can fix them: ORI-RN-005's write allowlist excludes `apps/example/**` and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/**` except its package.json; ORI-RN-001, ORI-RN-004 and ORI-AI-001 are completed. Behavior preservation is grounded in the landed code: apps/example's only theme control (`apps/example/gallery/chrome.tsx`) flips the app via `Appearance.setColorScheme` — exactly the signal `useColorScheme()` tracks — and the NativeWind consumer root (`packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/app/_layout.tsx`) already themes via `useColorScheme()`. After this lands, ORI-RN-005 reruns its blocked legs with no further work in its own files.

## How to verify

Run `pnpm exec tsx .tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-005-1/consumer-compile-proof.ts` — the task-owned scratch harness that materializes the prescribed consumer, copies the five canonical sources byte-identical (SHA-256 pairs), runs the consumer's `tsc --noEmit` (functional RED pre-fix with exactly the two named errors, GREEN post-fix), and records the preserved repository checks. Also run the preserved commands below.

## Scope

Own the two one-line fixes in `apps/example/components/live-chat-screen.tsx` and `packages/docs-snippets/nativewind/lib/theme.ts`, plus the scratch harness and bounded evidence under `.tmp/FIX-ORI-RN-005-1/`. On-device behavior remains ORI-RN-005's rerun and ORI-AI-002's matrix; every ORI-RN-005 in-flight file stays untouched.

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

# FIX-ORI-RN-005-1: Make the canonical live-chat sources compile in the independent NativeWind consumer

## What this does

Fixes the two compile defects that block ORI-RN-005's clean-consumer proof. In the prescribed independent NativeWind consumer — fresh Expo 57 root outside the monorepo from ORI-RN-001's committed template, registry items from the literal public recipe, the verified hook pins, and the five canonical app sources copied byte-identical — the consumer's own `tsc --noEmit` rejects with exactly two errors, both in landed files outside ORI-RN-005's write scope:

# Sprint 05: orient-search

**Status:** in_progress  
**Sequence:** 5  
**Timeline:** Phase 2

## Overview

Give a first-time integrator a complete orientation path: Introduction, one engine decision, registry-specific installation and CLI guidance, Theming and Dark mode, one seed-data Quickstart, and a handoff to a real AI SDK v7 example. Connect that content to persistent engine tabs, live theme values, built-site search, registry destinations, and useful missing-page recovery.

Absorb the smallest real prerequisites that make those paths executable: the published PromptInput import graph, both clean Expo consumers, a substantive ownership explanation, actual 404 recovery, the real example API and native composition, canonical registry hosting, and source-bound build and publication checks. This does not add another tutorial or a demonstrated use case. Sprint 06 may deepen the ownership tables; Sprint 11 may deepen resilience and accessibility; later delivery work may harden deployment and rollback.

The plan contains **36 tasks / 131 points**, compared with the roadmap sketch of approximately 12 items / 34–55 points: **76 points above its upper bound**. It retains 13 locked flows, 13 numbered gate steps, and four post-integration journey proofs. Estimates describe the approved prerequisite absorption rather than forcing the work into the sketch.

All implementation, functional RED, product verification, hosted acceptance, and deployment proof are future work. This document records a plan, not a passing gate or release.

## Human Testing Gate

**Gate:** A stranger opening /docs/introduction over the built site's local preview can read in one pass that the library provides universal AI chat and agent UI components for React Native, that it is distributed as a copy-paste registry, and that it is not an npm package.

**Entrypoint:** docs site local preview — built dist served by astro preview (http://localhost:4321) or the pnpm e2e:docs webServer; route /docs/introduction

**Before:** The source snapshot at the planned source SHA already contains Theming and shared layout, header, table, and tab controls. Introduction, Installation, CLI, Dark mode, Quickstart, the ownership-boundary route, and a custom 404 route are absent in that inspected snapshot. Existing Theming content still needs engine-correct claims and the real paired TokenTable. These are planning observations from the source, not current browser results. Each owner must observe the actual functional failure before implementation; the stale roadmap claim that all of these controls are absent is not a RED oracle.

**Success state:** A visitor reads useful, source-backed bodies instead of empty shells, chooses the correct engine once, follows literal registry commands, reads the same information without JavaScript, sees live theme changes without a flash, and reaches real content through keyboard search or missing-page recovery. The single Quickstart reaches a visible seed-data screen and then a separately verified real-provider example. Acceptance also requires the discriminating build checks and fresh native, provider, public-registry, and hosted evidence specified below.

**Demonstrates:** UC-DOCS-01, UC-DOCS-02, UC-SHELL-02, UC-SHELL-01 (TokenTable half), UC-SHELL-03 (prose-persistence half)

**Fixed carryover:** UC-GEND-07 AC-2; TR-12 (full); CAP-DOCS-01 snippet/link build integration. Boundary, recovery, API, and publication work support this projection; they do not expand the demonstrated-use-case list.

Mechanism: @ai-sdk/openai responses defaults store to true and converts every assistant text part carrying providerMetadata.openai.itemId into a bare item_reference whose content is NOT sent (apps/example/node_modules/@ai-sdk/openai/src/responses/convert-to-openai-responses-input.ts:606-610), so a stale itemId simultaneously drops the partial text and fails the request.

The client-side staleness signal is part.state: aborted turns leave text parts stuck at 'streaming' while completed turns end 'done' — this is what the sanitize keys on and it is the only reliable client-side discriminator.

The minimal AC-1 scenario as written (seed turn, stop backend, submit, restart, retry) does NOT reproduce the failure — a single completed turn plus endpoint loss retries successfully even pre-fix; an aborted mid-stream turn (or equivalent state damage) between them is the prerequisite, which is why the driver adds the aborted-essay leg.

Static or even type-only imports of apps/example modules (the hook via expo/fetch, and the ai/@ai-sdk/react dist d.ts themselves) add global DOM augmentations (HTMLElement | SVGElement unions) to the root tsc program and break unrelated spec files — any future driver touching these packages must runtime-load via computed specifiers with structural surfaces.

The published expo/fetch entry (expo/fetch.js requiring ./src/winter/fetch/index) cannot resolve in plain Node at all; only Metro resolves it, and its types live under expo/build/winter/fetch — which is why the lazy-import enabler works for types but must never be called headlessly.

Node's closeIdleConnections is more aggressive than the charter assumed: it destroys sockets with a received-but-unresponded request (an incomplete-body POST and even a not-yet-first-chunk proxied SSE both count as idle); only connections with an in-flight, headers-written response survive the sweep, which is exactly what the 20s bound plus closeAllConnections covers.

Playwright runs wrapped by the rtk hook buffer output and hang forever if the spawned astro preview outlives the run; killing the preview by its full command pattern (`astro.mjs preview` / `astro preview --host ... --port 4321`) is what unwedges them, and `rtk proxy` gives unbuffered real output for interactive runs.

A closed native <dialog> element stays in the DOM, so closed-state assertions must target the [open]-qualified selector or visibility, never element count; Pagefind 1.5.2 also indexes content inside hidden elements (the uniwind TabGroup panels are searchable) and loads its index chunks on the first query rather than at module import, so request-log assertions must separate the module phase from the chunk phase.

findings: Astro 7 (rolldown-vite) fails to bundle any static import from apps/docs that escapes the project root — probe-verified with gates.ts and token-map.ts at the identical depth — and unused aliased imports are tree-shaken before resolution, so naive probe builds silently skip resolution and lie about what works.

readdirSync({ withFileTypes: true }) reports symlinks as neither file nor directory, so a Dirent-based recursive copy silently drops the entire pnpm node_modules symlink fabric and the copied workspace dies at its first bin invocation; fs.cpSync preserves symlinks and copy-on-writes on APFS.

pnpm implicitly runs any prebuild script before build, so the 'public docs build' is really a four-stage chain (prebuild → registry:build → gallery:manifest → astro build) and failure triage must check the earliest stage.

Astro 7 scoped styles stamp data-astro-cid-* attributes onto plain elements, so the built page renders `<h1 data-astro-cid-...>` and text oracles over built HTML must match `<h1[^>]*>` and decode entities.

fallow reports stale suppressions, which makes a temporary ignore directive self-enforcing: the moment the suppressed finding stops firing (here, a future static import) the audit flags the directive and forces its removal.

findings: MDX program blocks only continue through import/export statements: a plain const or a JS block comment ends the ESM section and the remainder parses as prose (breaking the build at the first brace) — use export const declarations and {/* */} expression comments.

TabGroup named slots work from MDX via <div slot="engine"> children: the quickstart page is the repo's first MDX-to-TabGroup precedent (installation.mdx only uses InstallCommand, which wraps its slots internally in .astro).

spawnSync with a timeout kills the shell but orphans pnpm-to-tsx grandchildren — server-probe children need a supervised detached process group killed via process.kill(-pid) so the whole chain dies.

Playwright actionability semantics: clicking a control that is deliberately inert (the disabled send button) hangs until the test timeout, while dispatchEvent('click') fires the real DOM event and lets the disabled-control no-op be observed.

feedback: The task file's AC pinning would be stronger if plan-time validation ran pinned queries and selectors against the live generated dataset — 'exactly 1 matching row' and the keyboard phrasing both diverged from the real island contracts in ways the implementer had to derive and document.

The one-port-per-sprint topology worked only because agents communicated; making port ownership part of the dispatch contract (as the team-lead's briefing did) was the difference between a near-miss and a broken run — keep and enforce it for the remaining waves.
findings: A bare `page.screenshot({ path })` accepts exactly one path — the VIS-002-style multi-sink capture needs copyFileSync for the second sink, and a path array fails with 'unsupported mime type null' at capture time.

In this no-DOM-lib workspace, `locator.evaluate((el) => ...)` arrow callbacks fail pnpm typecheck — computed-style reads must be string page.evaluate expressions with result casts, matching the reading/token lanes' convention.

The ARIA tabpanel is a real Tab focus stop (TabGroup sets tabindex=0 on panels), so backward tabbing from the toolbar input lands on the visible panel before any tab — any keyboard test through the toolbar must expect and observe that stop.

AC phrasings like 'exactly 1 matching row' are fragile against a substring filter over generated descriptions — plan-time AC validation should run the pinned query against the dataset before pinning counts.
A full-width flex status line inside the toolbar needs an explicit order (here order:10 on the tabpanel) or it wraps between the tablist and the input, pushing the input to a second row.

Playwright's element screenshots/scrollIntoViewIfNeeded can disturb a scrollable's inner scrollLeft — set the wrapper's scrollLeft AFTER scrolling it into view and measure from the same evaluate tick.

From ORI-VIS-005's regression lane (not from this diff): not-found-search-recovery.spec.ts fails 2/13 on desktop+mobile pre-existing on trunk because VIS-003's merge (90cbe643) put the data-search-close button inside the [data-search-slot] mount, making '[data-search-slot] button' strict-mode ambiguous — already reported to the orchestrator with a one-line selector fix.

feedback: The ac-5 pattern — run the probe for real, capture the actual public state, then fail loudly as an unmet prerequisite with the owner named — kept the deployment dependency honest without a skip or a fake pass; it should be the standing template for deployment-dependent ACs.

Tasks whose predecessors pin exact DOM oracles (byte-equal text, region classes) should surface those pins in the dependency handoff's consumable form; I had to read ORI-AST-009's full spec to learn the explanation was already pinned to .page-header__description, which decided the whole composition.

Sibling-worktree preview arbitration needs a real protocol (per-worktree preview port or a lease file beside the strict-port guard); distinguishing a leaked PPID-1 preview from an in-flight run's webServer required manual ps inspection twice this cycle and one mistaken kill.
findings: The pre-fix 404 rendered the approved explanation twice in the emitted dist (verified: 2 occurrences in dist/404.html) because ORI-AST-009's spec pinned .page-header__description byte-equal but never asserted the manuscript text renders exactly once — presentation specs should assert copy uniqueness, not just presence.

ORI-VIS-003's merge 90cbe643 added data-search-close inside the [data-search-slot] mount (SearchDialog.astro:55), silently breaking ORI-AST-009's '[data-search-slot] button' selector while search-presentation.spec.ts's own 'button.search-dialog__trigger' pin stayed safe — cross-task selectors must target the element's own class, not a descendant-of-container shape.

A fresh browser context starts in the pre-paint default theme with localStorage rnr-theme unset, so a theme-persistence witness that only checks the class when already flipped polls null forever; the control must be made to write storage by real clicks.

Single-column geometry oracles must compare sibling regions to each other, not children against the container's border box: main.not-found's 1.5rem padding offsets every child by 24px and fails a 2px tolerance against the container's own x.

This repo's Playwright typings expose neither Locator.allBoundingBoxes nor expect.fail — use an nth(i).boundingBox() loop (protocol-level, works with JavaScript disabled) and a thrown Error for prerequisite failures.
